strengths: Modal focus management is complete and correct: a MutationObserver stack traps focus inside the topmost veil, restores it on close, and handles nested veils (e.g. chronicle over eulogy). All six dialog veils are covered.

aria-describedby on both the eulogy dialog (dName dSpan dEul dSurv) and the heir dialog (heirName heirTag heirInherit) so screen readers announce the full narrative content, not just the dialog label.

The #scene region is aria-live='assertive' aria-atomic='true', so the moment's prose is announced immediately to screen readers when a card appears — the single most important live-region call in the game.

The #flow pace control deliberately omits aria-pressed (it is a 3-state control, not a binary toggle) and carries the full state in the aria-label text, which is updated on every state change: 'the years are passing — tap to race ahead', 'the years are racing by — tap to return to the usual pace', 'time held still — tap to let the years resume'.
sr-only emotion prefixes (Joy, A loss, An echo) are injected via srTag() into both the ephemeral in-play log entries and the full memoir in the Chronicle, so colour is never the only differentiator.

WCAG AA contrast is met across the board: ink-dim (#a99c87) on the dark background (#16110d) is 6.36:1, well above 4.5:1; amber is 8.09:1; full ink is 13.14:1. The reflect button text (ink-dim) clears AA.

prefers-reduced-motion is honoured at two levels: CSS kills all transitions/animations via a blanket !important rule, and both scene.js and constellation.js read the media query at startup to freeze their animation clocks (dt=0 or throttled to 250ms).

The constellation keyboard interface is thorough: the tabpanel owns arrow-key traversal (Left/Right/Up/Down/Home/End), each chosen star is announced with age, choice text, alternative, and position ('Decision N of M') via a live region, and the canvas itself is aria-hidden.
The skip link is present, visible on focus, and targets #app correctly. It uses a smooth CSS transition rather than JavaScript.

The ARIA tablist pattern in the Chronicle is correctly implemented: roving tabindex, aria-selected, aria-controls, aria-labelledby, keyboard navigation with ArrowLeft/ArrowRight/Home/End, and focus moves with switchTab().

Touch targets meet 44px: footer buttons (.pp), delete confirm buttons (.delYes/.delNo), chronicle entry points (.chron/.chron2 with padding: 11px giving min-height 44px), eulogy secondary links (#dChron/#dBackup), and the inline delete button.

The stageA11y polite live region fires on every life-stage transition ('A new season of life: youth.') independently of the visual title animation — so screen readers get the announcement even when the CSS animation is suppressed.

The inline two-step delete confirm replaces native confirm() — focus lands on the 'delete' button, Escape disarms it, and both confirm/cancel have descriptive aria-labels ('Confirm: delete House X forever', 'Cancel: keep House X').

improvements.what: Add role='list' and role='listitem' to the .marks stat panel in the Chronicle (the four mark <div class='mark'> tiles), mirroring what is already done for #lineage and #slotList.
improvements.why: The four mark tiles (generations, lives lived, longest life, peak standing) are rendered as unlabelled divs with no list semantics — a screen reader traversing the panel gets four orphaned text nodes with no structural relationship. The fix is one setAttribute call on the .marks wrapper.

improvements.what: Add Escape-key dismissal to the eulogy (vDeath) and heir (vHeir) dialogs by adding them to the ESC_CLOSE map in the focus management IIFE.
improvements.why: The current ESC_CLOSE map covers vChron, vLoad, and vStock, but leaves vDeath and vHeir without keyboard dismissal. These are narrative gates (player must make a choice), so Escape should not skip the succession — but it could safely do nothing (preventDefault) or focus the primary action button, so the trap does not feel broken to screen reader users pressing Escape expecting a response.

improvements.what: Give the #log element role='log' (or remove role='button' and make the click handler a sibling control) to resolve the role tension.
improvements.why: #log simultaneously holds role='button' (so it is keyboard-activatable to open the Chronicle) and aria-live='polite' (so it announces incoming log lines). ARIA prohibits live regions on interactive roles — some browser/AT pairs will suppress the live announcements once the button role is applied. The cleanest fix is a transparent sibling <button> overlaid on the log that handles the click/keydown, leaving the log div as a pure live region.

verdict:
The accessibility implementation is genuinely thorough — correct focus trapping, assertive scene announcements, reduced-motion respected at two layers, full keyboard constellation traversal, AA contrast throughout, emotion prefixes for colour-blind users, and 44px touch targets everywhere — with only four minor residual gaps (log role tension,
-joined heir paragraphs, marks panel list semantics, and no Escape on the narrative gates), none of which block actual use.
